newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TAYLOR STAYS ON, BUT WAUGH IN THE WINGS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR STAYS ON, BUT WAUGH IN THE WINGS.

text.p: Australia kept faith with Mark Taylor on Thursday as captain for the forthcoming Ashes tour to England but the embattled opener conceded he could lose his job before the end of the test series unless his form improves.
Selectors chose burly left-hander Taylor to lead an experienced 17-man sqaud for the six-test series in England.
But they left the door open for Steve Waugh to take over during the tour by promoting the veteran all-rounder to vice-captain in favour of wicketkeeper Ian Healy.
Asked whether he could lose his job in England if he fails to rediscover his form, Taylor said: "I am a realistic person. That is a possibility."
"Everyone in Australian cricket knows that I have a lot of low scores recently. The fact that they (selectors) have stuck with me as a captain and as a player shows great faith in me."

Regarded as an outstanding tactician and team leader, Taylor failed repeatedly with the bat during the recent series wins against South Africa and West Indies. He has not notched up a test 50 since late 1995.
That slump in form has prompted a debate at home over Taylor's future, with former test bowling great Dennis Lillee calling on selectors to sack him.
Taylor told a news conference he expected to last out the tour: "I have been appointed for the tour of England and I'm looking forward to playing six test matches as captain."
Taylor said the selectors, in line with past practice, had not guaranteed he would lead his side throughout the test series in England.
"You never get told that. You are told you are captain for the tour, that's it. I have never been given a minimum or maximum period of captaincy," he said.
Healy's demotion was the biggest surprise in a squad containing only one player -- reserve wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist -- without test experience.
Healy became the first Australian to be suspended under the International Cricket Council's code of conduct when he was put out for two matches for dissent in South Africa.
Australia selectors dropped opener Matthew Hayden and pace bowler Paul Reiffel from the squad which completed a 2-1 test series defeat of South Africa.
Opener Michael Slater, dynamic young batsman Ricky Ponting and Queensland paceman Michael Kasprowicz were recalled.
Waugh, 31, captained Australia for the first time in a limited overs international against South Africa last week after Taylor stood down because of his lack of form.

Ponting was dropped after the second test against West Indies last December but shone in the domestic Sheffield Shield competition. Kasprowicz led the domestic tallies with 48 wickets, although the burly Queenslander went wicketless in his first two tests in the recent series against West Indies.
Slater began his test career in England in 1993 and averaged 47.41 before being dropped last year.

Under Taylor's aggressive leadership, Australia have become the unofficial world champions of test cricket, beating West Indies at home and away, South Africa away and England, Pakistan and Sri Lanka at home.
Squad:
Batsmen - Mark Taylor (captain), Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh (vice-captain), Matthew Elliott, Michael Slater, Ricky Ponting, Justin Langer.
All-rounders: Greg Blewett, Michael Bevan.
Wicketkeepers: Ian Healy, Adam Gilchrist.
Bowlers: Glenn McGrath, Jason Gillespie, Andy Bichel, Shane Warne, Michael Kasprowicz, Brendon Julian.
